metadata.title: Infrastructure reliability incident investigation
metadata.artifact_scope_note: Evidence is aggregated query output (not raw log lines or metric samples); it contains no chat/communication records.

incident_description: Reliability incident investigation of a production environment. Evidence consists of Elasticsearch aggregation results over application and proxy logs, Kubernetes, cloud-provider and host system events, Prometheus Alertmanager alerts, change-management / CI-CD audit records and metric anomaly detection. No root cause, impact or trigger is stated; these must be established from the supplied artifacts. Environment context: Organization: Bluepine Press (news and media publishing); Platform: AWS us-east-2 (zones us-east-2a/us-east-2b/us-east-2c); network range 10.148.0.0/16; Kubernetes cluster bluepi-prod-useast (EKS); Database: subscribers-db-01 holds subscribers records; Automation: data-retention workflows scheduled by Dagster and executed under service accounts (runs recorded with RUN- identifiers); Change management: production changes carry CR- identifiers.
investigation_questions: What change, deployment or automation run triggered the incident? Provide its change identifier.
Which code change introduced the faulty eligibility filter? Provide its change identifier.
Which file contained the faulty filter?
During what hour did the first signs of the failure appear? Provide the earliest date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC format.

What is the root cause category of the incident: configuration change, software defect, hardware failure, cloud provider failure, capacity exhaustion, automation error, certificate expiry, or third-party dependency failure?
Which of the three CIA components is primarily affected: availability, integrity, or confidentiality?
According to the error volume statistics, what single service emitted the most errors? Is it the root cause or a downstream symptom?
Which change is a red herring: recorded shortly before onset but unrelated to the failure? Give its identifier.
What change brought the service back to normal? Give its identifier.
